findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1876 is the Splunk Add-on for Amazon Web Services. No Splunk product is named 'Splunk Add-on for AWS S3'.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'Splunk Add-on for Amazon Web Services (Splunkbase 1876)', optionally adding '(S3 input)'.

findings.explanation: The Splunkbase listing for app 1546 is named 'REST API Modular Input' (`rest_ta`). It is a third-party app, not a Splunk-branded add-on.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'REST API Modular Input (`rest_ta`, Splunkbase 1546)' and say it is third-party.

findings.explanation: detailedImplementation says procurement spend is mapped to Categories 1–15 and lists Coupa and Oracle spend feeds. The SPL sets `scope3_category=1` for every Ariba row and never queries `coupa:spend_event` or `oracle:procurement_spend_event`.
findings.quote: **ariba:spend_event**, **coupa:spend_event**, **oracle:procurement_spend_event** rows with **toplevel_supplier_id**, UNSPSC_BUCKET, **amount_usd** mapped to GHG Protocol Scope 3 Category integers **1–15**
findings.suggested_fix: Describe only what the SPL does (Ariba spend, all as Category 1). Otherwise document that a UNSPSC-to-category lookup and Coupa/Oracle branches would have to be added to the search.

findings.explanation: These vendor API paths (repeated in detailedImplementation) look invented and none is cited. SAP Ariba APIs are served from openapi.ariba.com under product-specific paths, and Microsoft Sustainability Manager data is normally read through the Dataverse Web API (`/api/data/v9.x/msdyn_*`).
findings.quote: **`https://api.persefoni.com/v1/organizations/{orgId}/inventories`** ... Watershed **`/api/v1/measurements`** ... Sweep **`/api/v1/scope3/categories/{categoryId}/activities`** ... SAP Ariba **`/api/v1/procurement/spend-analysis/categories`** ... **Microsoft Sustainability Manager** **`/api/sustainability/v1.0/emissions`** ... **SAP Sustainability Footprint Management** **`/api/sustainability/v1/sfm/footprints`**
findings.suggested_fix: Check each vendor's API reference: Persefoni, Watershed, Sweep, SAP Ariba Analytical Reporting API, Microsoft Sustainability Manager on Dataverse, SAP SFM, EcoVadis. Replace each path with the documented one or drop it.

findings.explanation: The industry field should classify the industry; here it holds uncited statistics, some of them likely misattributed. The ~11.4× average and ~700× financed-emissions figures come from earlier CDP reports, not 2024 CDP or PCAF. The '~130× ocean versus air' GLEC figure in detailedImplementation is also uncited.
findings.quote: CDP Disclosure Insight Action 2024 cites apparel Scope 3 multiples ~24× Scope 1+2 versus portfolio averages ~11.4× ... (~700× operational baseline per PCAF 2024 narratives ) ... BCG-WEF Scope 3 Survey 2024 indicates organisations measure ~4.2 categories on average versus top-quartile ~11.5
findings.suggested_fix: Set `industry` to a plain value such as 'Cross-industry'. Drop the statistics or move them to references with the exact report and year confirmed.

findings.explanation: The SPL keeps no `inventory_period`, no prior-period total and no geography, and `Cat04` is not a field (the SPL uses `C4`). Dashboard Studio has no `splunk.choropleth` type: choropleths use `splunk.map` with a choropleth layer or `splunk.choropleth.svg`.
findings.quote: paired **`splunk.singlevalue`** portfolio **`portfolio_total_kg`** versus prior **`inventory_period`** ; ... optional **`splunk.choropleth`** when **`Cat04`** logistics splits geographies
findings.suggested_fix: Reference only fields the SPL outputs. Say a prior-period comparison needs a second search. Use the correct Dashboard Studio visualization type.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no `span=1h`. Maintenance windows, synthetic probes and 48-hour baselines do not apply to a weekly inventory Pareto report. The real causes of misleading hotspots are listed only in detailedImplementation Step 5.
findings.suggested_fix: List the real causes: the same supplier's emissions arriving from Persefoni, Watershed, Ariba EEIO and Climatiq at once; vendor-alias duplicates before `mdm_vendor_bridge.csv`; annual EEIO/DEFRA factor refreshes; Category 15 financed-emissions IDs colliding with supplier IDs; and suppliers missing from `supplier_engagement_scorecard.csv`, which defaults them to `tier=weak`.

findings.explanation: The search does not de-duplicate anything. It only displays a `double_count_symmetry_ok` flag from a lookup and sums every feed, so the promise of no double counting is not delivered.
findings.quote: so footprint totals stay honest across buyer and seller books without counting the same tonne twice
findings.suggested_fix: Say the report ranks suppliers by estimated emissions and flags where double counting still has to be checked.

findings.explanation: The reviewer is an automated agent and there is no record of SME sign-off, yet the UC carries unconfirmed API paths and the issues above.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until a sustainability or Splunk SME validates it.

findings.explanation: No Oracle Database telemetry is used. The `aws`, `oracle` and `salesforce` equipment tags are only loosely implied by optional feeds and are not monitored equipment.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `oracle_oracle_db` and keep equipment tags only for sources the SPL actually queries.

findings.explanation: WattTime marginal grid signals are not Scope 3 supplier emission factors, and listing every library at once hides which factor source this pipeline actually expects.
findings.quote: **factor_dataset_version** citing DEFRA Conversion Factors 2024, EPA GHGRP hubs, IPCC AR6 sector tables, ecoinvent v3.10 datasets, GLEC Framework v3.0 logistics intensities, WattTime marginal grid forecasts when geography permits
findings.suggested_fix: Name the factor libraries the organisation uses for each methodology and drop WattTime.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `multisearch` adds Persefoni inventory lines, Watershed measurements, Ariba spend multiplied by EEIO factors, and Climatiq estimates for the same suppliers without any de-duplication or source-precedence rule. `supplier_total_kg` and `portfolio_total_kg`, and therefore `cum_pct` and `pareto_band`, are inflated whenever more than one tool covers a supplier, which is the normal case when Persefoni already models Category 1 from the same spend.

The Watershed branch uses `coalesce(co2e_kg,measurement_mass_kg,"0")`. When `co2e_kg` is missing, a physical activity mass is summed as kg CO2e. Persefoni falls back from `methodology` to `data_quality_band` in the same way. Drop the non-equivalent fallbacks.
`eval scope3_category=1` labels all Ariba spend as Category 1. Spend on capital goods (Cat 2), freight (Cat 4), travel (Cat 6) and waste (Cat 5) is therefore misclassified.

The title promises '15 GHG-Protocol Categories', but `cat_label` keeps only C1, C4, C6 and C15 and collapses the other 11 categories into 'CX'. The Climatiq branch is the only one labelled 'hybrid'. The title overstates what the search reports.

summary: The UC describes a supplier Pareto hotspot report built by combining several carbon-accounting feeds. The SPL sums overlapping sources with no de-duplication, hard-codes all spend to Category 1, and collapses 11 of the 15 categories the title promises. The prose also carries a misnamed Splunkbase add-on, many unconfirmed vendor API paths, unsourced statistics, and verified status with no evidence.
